title: Guess two thirds of the average
objectives: Iterate best replies and see why real players stop early.

screens.title: Two thirds of the average
screens.prose: A room of players each write a number from 0 to 100. The winner is the one closest to two thirds of the average. Drag the average and watch its two thirds.
screens.question: What is the largest number that can ever be two thirds of the average?

hints.text: The average is largest when everyone writes 100.
Two thirds of 100.

feedback.correct: 66.67: two thirds of the largest possible average, 100.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Drag the average to its largest value and read two thirds of it.

byKey.hundred: 100 is the largest average. The target is two thirds of it.
byKey.half: 50 is the average of random guesses. The question asks for the largest target there could ever be.
byKey.third: 33.33 is two thirds of 50, a target for a random room. The largest average is 100, not 50.

explain.text: The average can be at most 100, so the target is at most $\tfrac23 \times 100 = 66.67$. A guess above 66.67 is beaten by 66.67 itself, whatever the others write. So no one should guess above it.

screens.title: Delete and look again
screens.prose: If no one guesses above 66.67, the average is at most 66.67 too. So the target can be at most two thirds of that.
screens.question: Fill in the bound after each round of deletion.

rows: Rounds until the bound is below 1

hints.text: Each round multiplies the bound by two thirds.
After $k$ rounds the bound is $100 \times (\tfrac23)^k$.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Multiply the last bound by two thirds each time.

byKey.r3c1: After 11 rounds the bound is 1.156, still above 1. The twelfth round takes it to 0.771.

explain.text: Each round the bound shrinks by two thirds: 66.67, 44.44, 29.63, 19.75, 13.17, and so on. The bound is $100(\tfrac23)^k$, so it drops below 1 after 12 rounds. In the limit every guess but 0 is deleted: 0 is the only equilibrium.

screens.title: Levels of thinking
screens.prose: Real rooms do not reach 0. Suppose a level-0 player guesses at random, so level-0 guesses average 50. A level-1 player best replies to a room of level 0. A level-2 player best replies to level 1.
screens.question: Fill in each level's guess.

hints.text: Level 1 guesses two thirds of level 0's average.
$\tfrac23 \times 50 = 33.33$.
33.33, 22.22, 14.81: each two thirds of the one before.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Each level guesses two thirds of the level below.

byKey.r1c1: Level 1 best replies to an average of 50: two thirds of 50 is 33.33.

explain.text: Level $k$ guesses $50 \times (\tfrac23)^k$: 33.33, 22.22, 14.81. Each level is one more round of deletion, started from 50. Experiments find most players stop after one to three levels.

screens.title: A real room
screens.prose: Here is a room: 30% level 0, 40% level 1, 20% level 2 and 10% level 3. Level-0 guesses average 50.

state.caption: A room of first-time players, as experiments often find.

screens.question: Find the room's average guess and the target.

hints.text: Weight each level's guess by its share.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Take the weighted average of the four guesses, then two thirds of it.

byKey.r0c1: Weight each guess by its share: 15 + 13.33 + 4.44 + 1.48 = 34.26.
byKey.r1c1: The target is two thirds of the average: $\tfrac23 \times 34.26 = 22.84$.

explain.text: The average is $15 + 13.33 + 4.44 + 1.48 = 34.26$, exactly $\tfrac{925}{27}$. The target is two thirds of it, $\tfrac{1850}{81} = 22.84$. That sits between level 2 and level 3.

screens.title: Your guess
screens.prose: You play once against the room above, a room of first-time players.

state.caption: A room of first-time players, as experiments often find.

screens.question: What do you guess?

options.why: You took deletion to its end. Against this room the target is near 23, so 0 loses to anyone near it.
You stopped after one step, which assumes everyone else guesses at random.
You deleted only the guesses that can never win. The room averages 34, not 100.

hints.text: The winner is closest to two thirds of what this room averages.
The last screen found the target: 22.84.
Guess about 23.

feedback.correct: About 23: two thirds of what this room will average.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Aim at the target this room produces.

byKey.b: You took deletion to its end. Against this room the target is near 23, so 0 loses to anyone near it.

explain.text: Zero is the equilibrium, but it wins only if everyone else reasons all the way down. This room averages 34.26, so the target is 22.84. The best guess is about two thirds of what this crowd will average.

screens.title: Only two players
screens.prose: Now only Ana and Ben play, still aiming at two thirds of the average. Suppose Ana guesses less than Ben.
screens.question: Which guess never loses?

options.why: 33 loses to any lower guess. With two players the lower guess always wins.
50 loses to any lower guess, since the target sits a third of the way along the sum.
0 is safe: it beats every positive guess and ties with another 0.

hints.text: The target is two thirds of $(a + b)/2$, which is $(a + b)/3$.
With $a = 20$ and $b = 60$ the target is 26.67, nearer Ana.
The lower guess always wins, so 0 never loses.

feedback.correct: 0: the lower guess always wins with two players.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Work out where the target lies between the two guesses.

byKey.b: 33 loses to any lower guess. With two players the lower guess always wins.

explain.text: The target is $(a + b)/3$. For $a < b$ its distance to $a$ is $|b - 2a|/3$ and to $b$ is $(2b - a)/3$, which is always larger. So the lower guess wins, and 0 can only tie.

screens.title: Iterated best replies
screens.prose:
Take a target of $p$ times the average, with $p < 1$. Round $k$ of deletion leaves guesses up to $100p^k$; level $k$ guesses $50p^k$:

$$\text{bound}_k = 100\,p^k, \qquad \text{level}_k = 50\,p^k$$

Every round deletes moves that are beaten whatever the others do.
screens.question: With $p < 1$, where does the deletion end?

options.why: That is the bound after one round. Each later round shrinks it again.
That is the level-1 guess, one step from random play. Deletion keeps going.
The room decides the best guess, but full deletion always ends at 0.

hints.text: Each round multiplies the bound by $p$.
$p^k$ tends to 0 when $p < 1$.
So only 0 survives.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Follow $100p^k$ as $k$ grows.

explain.text: Each round multiplies the bound by $p$, and $100p^k$ tends to 0. So with full reasoning every guess falls to 0. Real players stop after one to three steps, so the best guess is $p$ times what this crowd will average.

screens.title: Drill
screens.prose: Four questions, about three minutes each, as an interview allows. Say the reasoning aloud before you answer. Level-0 guesses still average 50.
screens.question: Fill in the four answers.

rows: Half the average: rounds of deletion until the bound is below 1
Half the average: the level-2 guess
Two thirds: a room of 50% level 0, 30% level 1, 20% level 2. The target?
Two thirds of the average, plus 10: the equilibrium guess

hints.text: Use $100p^k$, $50p^k$ and a weighted average.
For plus 10, everyone guesses the same $x$, and $x = \tfrac23 x + 10$.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Check the first answer that is marked.

byKey.r0c1: After 6 rounds the bound is 1.5625, still above 1. The seventh takes it to 0.78125.
byKey.r2c1: The average is $25 + 10 + 4.44 = 39.44$ and the target two thirds of it, 26.30.
byKey.r3c1: In equilibrium every guess equals the target: $x = \tfrac23 x + 10$ gives $x = 30$.

explain.text: Halving: $100 \times 0.5^7 = 0.78$, so 7 rounds, and level 2 is $50 \times 0.25 = 12.5$. The room averages $\tfrac{355}{9} = 39.44$, so the target is 26.30. With plus 10, $x = \tfrac23 x + 10$ gives 30.

screens.title: Follow-up: aim above the average
screens.prose: The interviewer flips the game: the target is 1.5 times the average, capped at 100. Fifty players take part.
screens.question: Which are equilibria? Select all that apply.

options.why: At 50 the target is 75, so each player gains by guessing higher.
At 66.67 the target is 100, so each player gains by moving up to it.

hints.text: Test each: if everyone guesses $x$, where is the target?
All 0: target 0. All 100: target capped at 100.
0 and 100 both hold; any $x$ in between has target $1.5x > x$.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. For each, compare the target with the common guess.

byKey.c: At 50 the target is 75, so each player gains by guessing higher.

explain.text: If all guess 0 the target is 0, and a lone deviator only moves away. If all guess 100 the target stays at the cap, 100, even if one drops lower. Keynes's beauty contest is the same: a market price is a guess about what others will pay.

ideas: No guess above two thirds of 100 can win; delete those, then repeat on what is left.
Full reasoning drives every guess to 0, the only equilibrium.
Real players stop after one to three steps, so guess two thirds of what this crowd will average.

formula.name: Rounds and levels
formula.note: For a target of $p$ times the average, $p < 1$.

summary.trap: Guessing the equilibrium, 0, against a room that does not reason all the way down.

quiz.prose: The target is three quarters of the average. Guesses run from 0 to 100.
quiz.question: What is the bound after two rounds of deletion?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Multiply 100 by three quarters, twice.

byKey.one: 75 is the bound after one round. Apply three quarters again.
byKey.level: That is the level-2 guess, which starts from 50. Deletion starts from 100.

explain.text: After one round the bound is 75, and after two it is $\tfrac34 \times 75 = 56.25$.

quiz.prose: The target is three quarters of the average. Level-0 guesses average 50.
quiz.question: What does a level-1 player guess?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Take three quarters of the level-0 average.

byKey.bound: 75 is three quarters of 100. Level 1 replies to an average of 50.

explain.text: A level-1 player best replies to a random room, which averages 50. Three quarters of 50 is 37.5.

quiz.prose: A large room plays two thirds of the average. You learn that everyone else will guess 30.
quiz.question: What do you guess?

options.why: Matching the room puts you 10 above the target, which is two thirds of 30.
0 is the equilibrium, but this room averages 30, so the target is 20.
You took two thirds twice. The others are fixed at 30, so the target is 20.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find the target this room produces.

explain.text: In a large room your guess barely moves the average, which stays near 30. The target is two thirds of 30, which is 20. So guess 20.
